text:
mel: Quick sync — I'm kicking off a short RFC for a 'mode-compatibility checker' + migration playbook. Primary problem: customers see subtle manifest/feature diffs when moving hosted->private (KMS, secret surface, prefix caching) and we end up with ops tickets. Want a small CLI that fails fast and gives actionable remediation steps.
sam: +1. happy path would be a single command that flags unsupported keys and suggests replacements.
jordan: Are we talking static schema diff only or runtime probes too?
mel: Both ideally. Start with static manifest checks (required fields, deprecated flags, auth surfaces). Then an optional probe mode that runs lightweight API calls against the target control plane to validate secrets/KMS access, model pull, and runtime kernel flags.
anya: Will this need to know hosting-mode semantics? e.g., hosted allows shared KMS token flow, private must use customer KMS + rotate window.
mel: Exactly. Checker should load a mode profile (hosted/dedicated/private) and apply rules. Profiles encode: allowed secret types, required roles, disallowed fields, telemetry endpoints, and a short remediation blurb.
sam: UX idea: exit code 0 = pass, 1 = warnings only, 2 = failures. Print short guidance and a `--dump-playbook` option to generate a one-page migration checklist.
jordan: For probes we need a safe auth flow. Maybe we support an ephemeral probe token that only reads manifests and tests KMS encrypt/decrypt with a test blob. No model inferences.
mel: Good constraints. Also add a policy for sensitive checks: default probe is off, opt-in with `--probe`. CPs will need a small probe endpoint that can validate pull permissions.
anya: Who owns rule definitions? It should live in infra repo as YAML with versioning so product/rd can add rules without code change. We can wire it into our controlplane config bundles.
sam: Implementation sketch: small Go binary, rule evaluator, profile loader, probe harness that uses existing controlplane clients. CLI example:
```
$ redwood-compat-check --profile private --manifest ./service.fcd.yaml
WARN: key `enable_public_acls` is not supported in private; use `allowed_vpcs`
FAIL: KMS alias arn:aws:kms:... not accessible by tenant-role. Run `rdwctl grant-kms-access` or follow playbook generated at ./compat-playbook.md
```
jordan: Nice. How do we handle host-specific defaults? e.g., hosted has implicit prefix caching enabled, private might require explicit cache config. Rules need to capture defaults vs required settings.
mel: We'll include a `defaults` section per profile and rule semantics describe whether they target missing keys (required), forbidden keys (disallowed), or divergent defaults (mismatch).
anya: Telemetry/observability note: the playbook should also tell SRE what dashboards/queries to run post-migration — token cost, latency P50/P95, cache hit rate. Add that as optional `--observability` output.
sam: Add ties to rollout strategy: if a manifest change is non-blocking we return a migration plan with canary steps + rollback markers. e.g., change `kv_cache.enabled: true` -> plan: canary 5% for 1h, monitor hit rate > 70%, then ramp.
jordan: For private, we should include operator steps for secrets (rotate keys, verify HSM bindings). Maybe the checker can emit a short bash snippet for common steps.
mel: Agreed. Minimal example snippet for KMS grant will be part of the playbook.
anya: Security: must never echo plaintext secrets in output. Also playbook artifacts stored locally only, with a flag to `--upload-playbook` to an S3 bucket (customer or our audit store) with proper ACL.
sam: Who will own the initial rule set? I volunteer infra for the first pass, then hand off maintenance to platform.
mel: Thanks. Proposal next steps: I will draft a short RFC with scope, MVP rules, and an example manifest set. Action items: mel to draft RFC by EOD Friday; sam to prototype CLI skeleton; jordan to design probe contract; anya to outline observability checklist.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: infra/compat-checker/prototype -> staging at 1783461200, status: started
mel: ping when staging build is up, I'll wire it into the docs and the internal quickstart.
jordan: One more ask — include a `--strict-version` toggle to enforce controlplane schema versions; helpful for long-running private installs.
mel: Good call. Adding to RFC. Thanks all :rocket:
